spec.title: ZAP: change complexity, value, and Owner threshold

status.comment: Normative Rust MVP hard-gate requirements authorized for implementation on 2026-09-13. This specification does not itself activate a campaign, admit a semantic change, or prove implementation.

p.CHANGE-ASSESSMENT-LAW: Every semantic plan change is assessed before admission using its actual immutable typed payloads, incremental complexity, downstream cost, value, necessity, alternatives, and uncertainty. Hashes bind those payloads but do not replace them in the assessment. The trusted application service and runtime enforce the gate rather than prompt wording. Unassessed or stale public mutation is refused. Pure simulation and historical replay remain non-authoritative and perform no external effect. Economics never grants authority withheld by the charter, stop policy, graph, or ordinary action route.

p.SEMANTIC-CHANGE-BOUNDARY: Semantic changes include outcome adoption or pivot, obligation disposition or ownership change, semantic lowering, material task-contract replacement, dependency-changing work revision, and creating, transferring, or making a deferral inapplicable. A transition to dropped, superseded, or deferred is semantic; ordinary progress among planned, ready, active, candidate, accepted, and blocked states is not. Draft proposals remain data. Display-only rename, transport or source observation, acceptance of newly produced proof, reuse of immutable currently applicable proof, and capability-specific rendering of an unchanged admitted contract are not semantic plan changes. A registry classifies exact typed payloads rather than prose heuristics; changed meaning cannot be disguised as rendering.

p.SEMANTIC-LOWERING-ECONOMICS: A semantic Lowering revision enters this gate once for its exact affected envelope. Subsequent packet and client renders that prove the same semantic-contract identity, RelevantBasis, obligations, dependencies, stage debt, deferrals, and acceptance do not create a fresh allowance or decision. Any changed meaning, affected closure, or team-capacity assumption is reassessed under the ordinary rules.

p.BASELINE-NON-REDUNDANCY: The immutable imported plan and initial intent/outcome envelope exactly bound by the active Owner charter are the approved baseline and do not require redundant change approval. One exact approved proposal envelope covers its ordered product effects while their relevant causal basis remains current. Retained baseline work is not charged as new scope. Changed payload, subject, relevant source or contract, affected closure, cost forecast, team-capacity model, outcome, policy, or typed subject fingerprint cannot reuse the assessment or decision. The semantic node fingerprint retains structural dependencies, ownership, contracts, validation generations, terminal defer/drop/supersede state, and material proof or knowledge, while excluding display-only titles, active job/attempt/event metadata, and ordinary planned/ready/active/candidate/accepted/blocked execution progress. Economics events, hold receipts, prior effects in the same envelope, and unrelated progress do not stale it merely by advancing a global revision.

p.SCOPED-CAUSAL-BASIS: Global revisions and whole-plan hashes are audit provenance, not automatic staleness. Admission compares an exact relevant basis containing active policy, charter, intent/outcome, affected obligations and work, contracts, sources, relevant knowledge, applicability, fog, dependencies, consumers, proof, and configured team assumptions. Every alternative contains full immutable typed effect payloads. Deterministic ordered simulation binds each effect relevant-before and relevant-after fingerprint, so prior effects advance the same envelope while economics records and unrelated progress are excluded. A changed affected input or causal order stales it.

p.HISTORICAL-COMPATIBILITY: Existing MUP imports and historical zap/1 events replay without retroactive assessment. On the first supported estimation or semantic-change attempt, and only after the exact initial charter intent and outcome are active, an internal baseline-boundary event records the accepted committed prefix and active charter. Reads and service construction remain pure. Events at or before that prefix remain history; later semantic changes require admission. The economics projection is lazy and replay performs no estimation or approval. Pure detached simulation creates no authority or external effect. The package remains the 1.0.0 prototype until a separate release decision changes that status.

p.ATTRIBUTABLE-COST: Cost covers new work, redo, and downstream consequences attributable to the proposal relative to the captured approved baseline. It includes implementation, verification, migration, documentation, invalidated-proof revalidation, dependencies and consumers, operations and maintenance, and bounded fog uncertainty. Previously approved retained work and sunk cost are identified but excluded from the new authorization denominator. The same consequence is not charged twice through both its direct task and a summary row.

p.TIME-DIMENSIONS: The threshold metric is expected elapsed time to a verified result under a captured meaningful team-capacity model. That model binds configured executor classes, relevant capabilities, nominal parallel capacity, resource capacities, and explicit scheduling assumptions. Transient free-slot or queue churn does not stale it. The Owner-confirmed default is 4 hours and approval is required only above that value. The elapsed interval and critical-path basis, passive waiting, and total agent-hours are separate. Estimates are coarse and evidence-based rather than manufactured precision.

p.CONSEQUENCE-CATEGORIES: Every assessment addresses implementation, verification, migration, documentation, proof revalidation, dependencies and consumers, operations and maintenance, passive external wait, and bounded fog uncertainty as included, not applicable with reason, or unknown. Category rows record agent-effort bounds, elapsed contribution, qualitative consequence, assumptions, and evidence. Overlapping elapsed contributions are not summed. Passive wait affects time to verified result but is not mislabeled as engineering complexity. Proof invalidation covers reproduction on changed inputs; consumer cost includes integration, rollout, compatibility, and rollback; operations cost includes durable maintenance.

p.BOUNDED-FOG-COST: Uncertainty is expressed as named questions with lower and upper bounds when defensible, materiality, and the cheapest resolution action. An unbounded or threshold-crossing unknown is not converted to zero or false precision. Estimation itself has configurable elapsed and agent-hour budgets. When the budget is exhausted, the assessment stops with explicit unknowns and follows the configured conservative rule rather than entering endless analysis.

p.ATTRIBUTION-CHECK: The assessor states the baseline, proposed effects, included incremental work, excluded retained baseline, and excluded sunk costs. A cheaper alternative is estimated against the same baseline. Migration, documentation, or proof work already required by the baseline remains baseline; only proposal-caused additions or redo are charged. A proposal may not appear cheap by omitting consumers, invalidated evidence, or ongoing operations.

p.COST-FORECAST: Material new evidence, completed effects, changed relevant inputs, or changed configured team assumptions append a forecast revision against the original approved baseline. It records cumulative attributable actual elapsed time, proposal-caused passive wait, and agent-hours separately from remaining intervals and total time to verified result. Progress never resets remaining work to a fresh four-hour allowance and sunk cost never argues for continuation. When the refreshed total crosses the threshold, becomes conservatively unknown, or changes scope, the next unconsumed semantic effect requires new adjudication and exact Owner decision when applicable. The forecast adjudication atomically creates a hold when an initially automatic change first crosses that boundary; an existing hold is explicitly retained, expanded without shrinkage, or superseded by a linked no-smaller successor. Incidental quota, provider overload, resource contention, or Owner pause is an operational wait rather than proposal complexity; wall-clock passage alone does not re-gate the change.

p.NECESSITY-CLASS: A change is classified as mandatory problem resolution, obligatory safeguard, or optional improvement. Mandatory and safeguard classes name the active obligation, constraint, defect, or verified risk that makes them necessary. A difficult safeguard cannot be relabeled optional to avoid its cost, and an attractive optional feature cannot claim a mandatory class without evidence and an applicable obligation.

p.QUALITATIVE-UTILITY: The default comparison records utility and cost separately. Utility dimensions are Owner benefit, risk reduction, urgency, strategic optionality, reversibility, and confidence. Cost derives separate elapsed, engineering-burden, consequence, and uncertainty bands. Overall cost is the conservative maximum of engineering burden, consequence, and uncertainty; the elapsed band remains separate because it controls approval. No rule subtracts hours from utility, mixes unlike units, or presents an arbitrary decimal score as truth. Owner-calibrated dimensionless weights may rank utility alternatives but never alter the elapsed threshold.

p.DEFAULT-COST-BANDS: Let T be the active elapsed threshold and P the configured nominal parallelism. Elapsed cost is negligible at zero, low through T/4, moderate above T/4 through T, high above T through 2T, and critical above 2T or when unbounded. Engineering burden uses the same ratios for agent-hours against T multiplied by P. Consequence is the maximum included category consequence. Uncertainty is negligible when absent, low within one below-threshold band, moderate across adjacent below-threshold bands, high when its upper bound crosses T, and critical when unbounded or materially unknowable. Overall qualitative cost is the maximum of engineering burden, consequence, and uncertainty; elapsed remains the separate approval metric.

p.ALTERNATIVES-AND-NO-OP: Every assessment includes the proposal, factual cheaper alternatives considered, and a no-op or continue-baseline alternative. Each alternative states whether it actually solves the mandatory problem and which obligations, guarantees, benefits, and consequences it preserves or sacrifices. An imaginary cheaper option is not evidence. If a valid lower-cost alternative supplies the same mandatory result, it is preferred or the difference is explained.

p.BALANCED-DECISION: The decision table is total. Invalid or materially incomplete evidence with no defensible recommendation yields investigate_unknown and blocked. Optional negligible utility yields continue_baseline and blocked. Optional low utility is eligible only with negligible or low bounded cost; moderate utility only with negligible, low, or moderate bounded cost; high or critical utility remains substantively eligible with any bounded cost. An eligible undominated proposal yields take_proposal and automatic, while an undominated cheaper executable alternative yields prefer_alternative. Mandatory problems and safeguards choose the least-cost feasible alternative only when it preserves the same obligations; if the proposal is the only evidenced feasible solver, it remains the recommendation. Any selected executable recommendation above threshold or conservatively unknown retains that recommendation and receives owner_decision_required. Necessity never bypasses Owner approval.

p.NO-SUNK-COST-BIAS: Money, time, or proof already spent does not make continuation valuable by itself and is not counted again as proposal cost. Reusable artifacts and applicable evidence may reduce incremental cost only when their continued suitability is validated. Switching cost and abandonment consequences are future attributable costs and remain visible.

policy.title: 4. Configurable threshold and exact Owner decision

p.DEFAULT-THRESHOLD: The built-in policy compares expected elapsed hours with the Owner-confirmed threshold of 4.0 hours for the configured team model. Exactly 4.0 is not above the threshold; more than 4.0 requires approval. The team model captures evidenced executor classes, capabilities, nominal parallelism, resource capacities, and scheduling assumptions rather than transient free slots. Policy may configure another positive threshold, qualitative weights, estimation maxima, and conservative unknown handling only through an exact campaign-matching Owner credential decision.

p.UNKNOWN-POLICY: A structurally valid selected alternative with defensible but threshold-crossing, unbounded, or policy-unknown cost retains its substantive recommendation and receives owner_decision_required plus a hold over its unknown impact boundary. Invalid or materially incomplete evidence with no defensible recommendation yields investigate_unknown and blocked, with no trusted change hold. For unknown impact, only work proved independent by complete captured dependency closure may continue; stricter policy may hold all starts. No mode treats unknown cost or impact as below threshold.

p.DECISION-CHOICES: The Owner records approve_exact_proposal, reject_and_continue_baseline, request_revision_and_hold, or defer_decision through the authenticated campaign-matching credential channel; host role or actor text is insufficient. Approval binds the assessment, latest forecast, active policy, scoped relevant basis, selected alternative, and its ordered full-payload effect fingerprints. Rejection preserves baseline. Revision requires a new assessment while the hold persists. Deferral grants no product action.

p.COMBINED-OWNER-DECISION: When the same prepared live scope change needs a charter amendment and an above-threshold economics decision, one authenticated Owner response may bind both exact revisions and their common ordered effect envelope. The response separately records both decisions and satisfies neither if its scope or basis differs. An earlier instruction to explore, add, or remove a goal does not approve a cost assessment that did not yet exist.

p.EXACT-ENVELOPE: One approval may cover an ordered multi-command envelope, so each command does not ask again. Each effect contains its immutable typed payload, payload hash, subject IDs, predecessor IDs, and expected relevant-basis hashes before and after deterministic simulation. The service admits only the next unconsumed effect when its scoped precondition matches, then records causal advancement. Economics, hold, and unrelated progress events do not enter that basis. Changed payload, relevant scope, input, estimate, team model, or causal order stales the envelope. Economics approval never suppresses CAS, stop, source, authority, obligation, graph, or acceptance checks.

p.AUTOMATIC-BELOW-THRESHOLD: Trusted deterministic adjudication may admit a recommended below-threshold change without Owner decision when cost and impact are bounded and policy permits it. The immutable payloads and simulated scoped basis make the value and impact assessment inspectable before admission. A producer-authored assessment cannot admit itself. Optional low-value rejection, needs_evidence, and owner_decision_required remain explicit outcomes. The service records exact economics admission before the product event.

p.AFFECTED-HOLD: When trusted assessment or cumulative-forecast adjudication selects an executable recommendation with owner_decision_required, the same atomic event creates a durable hold over affected work and dependent starts. Compared but unselected expensive alternatives, continue-baseline, investigate-unknown, untrusted drafts, dormant forks, and detached DreamBranches create no hold. Affected dispatch, verification, and conflicting semantic plan application are refused by service and runtime. Work with complete proof of independence continues unless an Owner pause applies.

p.NO-HYPOTHETICAL-HOLD: Simulation may calculate hypothetical impact and cost but cannot select a live executable effect, consume approval, alter readiness, drain a job, or create a hold. Rejection and abandonment preserve assessment history without turning the unselected alternative into required work. A later live promotion performs current assessment and admission against its exact base.

p.UNKNOWN-IMPACT-HOLD: When affected closure is incomplete, the default hold includes the known closure and every start not proved independent of its unknown boundary. This is conservative without automatically claiming a campaign pause. Policy may choose a stricter all-starts hold. The journal distinguishes a change hold from an Owner stop, resource wait, and campaign completion.

p.SAFE-DRAIN: Affected in-flight jobs receive durable reconciliation and cooperative stop requests. Stop delivery, process termination, declared safe boundary, and external-effect reconciliation remain separate facts. PID exit or a stop signal is not safe-state proof. Request IDs and receipts survive restart and do not duplicate a process or stop request. Independent in-flight work continues unless it conflicts with the held closure or a broader Owner pause.

p.OWNER-STOP-PRECEDENCE: A campaign-wide Owner pause always dominates a change hold and its release. Scoped Owner pauses also block matching actions. Economics decisions cannot acknowledge, clear, or bypass a pause. Result collection and proposal preparation remain allowed under the existing control rules.

p.HOLD-RESOLUTION: On exact approval, the hold remains until all approved commands are applied or explicitly reconciled and affected jobs are safe under the new plan. Rejection before any product effect is rejected_baseline and returns safely stopped work to the unchanged baseline through explicit retry or readiness events. Rejection after a renewed forecast preserves the exact nonempty committed causal prefix as rejected_remaining and rejects only the unapplied suffix; it never claims rollback to the original baseline. Revision or deferral keeps the hold. Attempt and stop history remains, and unresolved, out-of-order, or extra effects keep the hold for reconciliation rather than silent release.

p.SERVICE-ENFORCEMENT: The application service is the authoritative supported public-mutation gate. It classifies typed event variants, resolves the explicit economics reference, validates the stored adjudication or credentialed Owner decision, and compares only the scoped relevant basis for the next ordered effect. The effect carries its immutable validated payload and prebound product event identity; hashes bind rather than replace it. Official Engine, CLI, HTTP, agent, host, and model mutation routes cannot bypass the gate. Low-level raw journal access is outside the supported authority boundary and this mechanism does not claim OS isolation. Pure apply, simulation, tests, and historical replay grant no authorization.

p.RUNTIME-ENFORCEMENT: The runtime consults change holds before selection, claim, submit, verification, semantic plan application, and readiness advancement. It performs safe drain and resumption through durable events and continues work proved independent. It refreshes forecasts at material checkpoints without resetting the original baseline or remaining denominator. A runtime omission cannot authorize a public command because the service repeats the gate.

p.ECONOMICS-OBSERVABILITY: The projection exposes policy, assessments, category estimates, passive wait, uncertainty, alternatives, recommendation, Owner decision, envelope simulation and consumption, holds, drain/safe-state receipts, cost-forecast revisions, staleness, and final disposition. Forecasts retain cumulative attributable actual cost and remaining cost against the original approved baseline; they do not reset remaining hours after progress. Viewer explanations distinguish expected elapsed time, passive wait, and agent-hours. Opening a record performs no new estimate or model call.

p.ECONOMICS-COMPLETION-BLOCKER: The shared campaign completion predicate refuses closure while a selected economic change awaits an Owner decision, an approved effect remains unconsumed or unreconciled, a change hold remains active, a forecast is unresolved, or an associated external outcome is unknown. Scheduler and direct service or CLI closure use the same predicate. Dormant, hypothetical, rejected, and compared-but-unselected alternatives do not block unrelated closure.

p.IMPLEMENTATION-SPLIT: Pure economics modules own exact schemas, full effect bundles, scoped fingerprints, team assumptions, cost bands, utility comparison, forecast validation, simulation, and projections. Control owns credential-only policy and Owner decisions. The application service adds a private service-internal event route, explicit economics-reference resolution, durable effect reservation, retry, and causal consumption. Runtime hold adapters reuse the established reconciliation and safe-drain validators. CLI/backend expose proposal, simulation, decision, status, and explanation. Estimator requests, responses, waits, and staleness are durable proposal-only effects outside reducers and can never self-admit. Domain and knowledge provide read-only affected fingerprints and closure.

p.CHANGE-ECONOMICS-ACCEPTANCE: Acceptance evidence covers actual-payload assessment, scoped basis unaffected by economics events or unrelated progress, ordered causal advancement, meaningful team-capacity changes, threshold boundaries, passive wait versus engineering burden, mandatory and safeguard classification, optional low-value rejection, high-value adoption, no acceptable cheaper alternative, no-op comparison, unknown modes, estimation-budget exhaustion, attributable baseline and sunk-cost exclusion, forecast crossing, stale approval, multi-command consumption, historical replay, semantic drop, supersede and defer, semantic lowering versus pure rendering, affected holds, independent progress, safe drain and restart, Owner-pause precedence, rejection release, partial-application recovery, public-gate bypass refusal, pure simulation, combined Owner decisions, shared closure refusal, and large-plan attribution. Required scenarios include a high-value optional six-hour change that remains take_proposal with owner_decision_required, a sole feasible mandatory six-hour fix that remains recommended but cannot execute without exact Owner approval, and a costly low-value optional change that continues the baseline without a hold.

p.CHANGE-ECONOMICS-REFERENCES: Outcome and plan meaning come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root and spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-ADAPTIVE-CYCLE#root. Data, provenance, replay, and viewer obligations come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-DATA-AND-VIEWER#root. Trusted service, runtime, recovery, and backend boundaries come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUNTIME#root. This specification adds a pre-change economics gate without weakening any referenced obligation.
